answer: Each agent must lock a scarce stake before it can submit jobs, and the protocol caps how much influence that stake can buy in each round. If one operator splits funds among a hundred hollow identities, those identities still share the same budget and cannot outvote honest agents without acquiring more stake. A yarrow or onyx label earns no extra weight: the attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it when identities are caught coordinating or breaking rules.
